newsitem.title: USA: Disney shares rise on Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: Disney shares rise on Q4 results.

text.p: Shares of Walt Disney Co rose nearly 3.5 percent Tuesday after the company reported better than expected fiscal fourth quarter profits.

The Burbank, Calif.-based entertainment company posted a profit of $336 million, or $0.49 a share, versus $265 million, or $0.50 a share, a year ago. The number of shares outstanding rose to 685 million from 533 million a year ago.
The First Call consensus earnings estimate for the fourth quarter, ended September 30, was $0.48 a share.
Disney was up 2-1/2, or 3.4 percent, to 76.

Disney's fourth quarter proforma profit, which assumes the company owned Cap Cities/ABC for both the fiscal 1996 and fiscal 1995 fourth quarters, rose to $354 million, or $0.52 a share, from $221 million, or $0.32, a year earlier.
Chuck Hill, director of research for First Call, said most analysts were using proforma estimates, meaning Disney's profit of $0.52 a share was $0.04 higher than the consensus estimate.
Smith Barney analyst Jill Krutick said all three of Disney's divisions -- creative content, broadcasting and theme parks -- posted better-than-expected results.
She said the improvement in Disney's Broadcasting division, which reported a 36 percent jump in proforma operating income for the quarter, was largely driven by accounting benefits.
Creative Content, which reported a 31 percent rise in proforma operating income, benefited from strong live action films during the quarter, she said.
Disney's theme park business also turned in a strong quarter, with attendance up an estimated seven to nine percent and pricing up about two percent, Krutick said.
Looking forward, she said the outlook for Disney was bright, with Theme Parks and Creative Content performing well and Broadcasting presenting "major challenges."
